anomaly_alerts.description: oai-nrf network_rx_mbps dropped to 0.01 Mbps (z=7.6) while CPU and memory utilization are at 0 %, indicating the NRF is not receiving any traffic.
anomaly_alerts.suggested_cause: NRF pod appears idle – likely a loss of upstream connectivity (e.g., UPF or other VNFs not routing registration traffic) or a mis‑configuration that prevented the NRF service from binding to its network interface, causing zero CPU/memory usage and no inbound packets.
suggested_actions: Inspect NRF pod logs for startup errors or service‑binding failures
Verify NRF container network namespace and interface IP assignment
Check connectivity from UPF, AMF, and other VNFs to the NRF (ping, telnet on port 80/443)
Confirm NRF registration endpoints are reachable via service discovery (K8s DNS)
Review recent configuration changes or deployments that might have altered network policies or service mesh rules
If needed, restart the NRF pod and monitor metrics for recovery
